key_insight: A small independent checker converts admissible potential and exactly charge-conserving current fields into guaranteed error bounds for PDE outputs from conventional solvers, LLM-written code, and neural surrogates.
engineering_relevance: Solver-independent certificates can expose errors that convergence studies miss and provide per-prediction reliability bounds for automated simulation pipelines.
method: Require solver outputs to include an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current.
Check these fields against a written physics specification to bound error.
Evaluate conventional, deliberately buggy, LLM-written, and neural solvers on the same problem.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted all five convergent buggy solvers; reduced-basis neural predictions received bounds at most 0.0021% wide in-range and 0.3–25% wide out-of-range, where 90% conformal intervals covered none of 14 tests.
watch_item: Guarantees apply to the stated model, but informative bounds require energy-accurate outputs on a resolving grid; free-nodal neural outputs produced valid yet uninformative bounds.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
